<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="8b02427e-c92b-457d-a3f9-197d31afc747">nested loop</dfn>

Consists of an outer loop and one or more inner loops. Each time the outer loop is repeated, the inner loops are reentered, and all required iterations are performed.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="13709ead-eba6-4f39-bed3-4d91de20a780">off-by-one error</dfn>

Occurs when the loop is executed one more or one less time than it should have been

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e2cee64b-5f96-4e16-85fe-f4a4c18199a2">output redirection</dfn>

Changes console output to a file

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f5445b9a-e978-4f7a-861e-d0a5f8fcd4e6">posttest loop</dfn>

The loop continuation condition is checked after the loop body is executed

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="438f2192-6872-4cf7-be09-52bce417d7ae">pretest loop</dfn>

The loop continuation condition is checked before the loop body is executed

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="5253279c-de72-46a9-be3e-40ec5f26d960">sentinel value</dfn>

Signals the end of the input

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f9145161-7b54-42dc-a825-de0b84d112cc">while loop</dfn>

A loop construct that begins with the keyword while

# Chapter 6

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="0f49a38a-7fb6-43c8-a52a-50509ebec3b4">actual parameter (i.e., argument)</dfn>

The variables or data to substitute formal parameters when invoking a function

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="4c152c2d-0c0c-48db-84fc-eed7f2c1dffc">ambiguous invocation</dfn>

Occurs when there are two or more possible functions to match an invocation of a function and neither is more specific than the other(s).

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="585f81f8-fc13-4686-b907-740ddd3a9ac9">argument</dfn>

See "[actual parameter](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DB4E)"

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="5ded4b12-7502-4c48-9bd2-ab4e4ae6cb53">automatic variable</dfn>

Local variables

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f90e6a92-cde4-4b2a-ab61-adbeee4c0e7b">bottom-up implementation</dfn>

Testing functions incrementally from the bottom moving upward along the chain of the functions

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="6b754fcf-3a43-4fe2-a05c-900431ba8471">call-by reference</dfn>

See "[pass-by reference](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DB90)"

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="793794c1-d5c0-4913-ac62-7b33339fcce0">call-by value</dfn>

See "[pass-by value](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DB93)"

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a83c991b-b8da-418f-9430-1ed7583af2f1">divide and conquer</dfn>

The concept of function abstraction can be applied to the process of developing programs. When writing a large program, it is recommended to use this strategy to decompose the program into subproblems. The subproblems can be further decomposed into smaller, more manageable problems.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a5d5e730-fac3-4d3a-99dc-c008271c0a65">formal parameter (i.e., parameter)</dfn>

The variables defined in the function signature

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="da0847f1-867a-4458-847e-8dc365b8286d">function</dfn>

A collection of statements grouped together to perform an operation. See class function; instance function.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f559f47a-b4d9-4f40-9107-2ab39ebc7011">function abstraction</dfn>

A technique in software development that hides detailed implementation. Function abstraction is defined as separating the use of a function from its implementation. The client can use a function without knowing how it is implemented. The client program will not be affected if the implementation changes.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="90e82a6e-7b55-4453-8502-85658d380300">function declaration</dfn>

Includes a header without the implementation

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="5f69d372-6e65-4383-a432-bbf73af3ba21">function header</dfn>

Includes the return type and the signature of a function

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="39c75681-c299-49f2-aad6-8814668c8f41">function overloading</dfn>

Functions in the same class can be defined with the same name as long as there is enough difference in their parameter profiles.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="ac91181a-0fad-4784-a44a-5bdbbfbfdf3a">function prototype</dfn>

Complete function declaration with body

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="72433ec0-7fe8-432a-b10d-afe0e73e9662">function signature</dfn>

The combination of the name of a function and the list of its parameters

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b1afdfed-334f-40d6-9b20-48264a4f0221">global variable</dfn>

A variable declared outside all functions and is accessible to all functions in its scope

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="950b2e68-3d36-4d4c-adf9-102c22c0ba6c">information hiding</dfn>

A software engineering concept for hiding the detail implementation of a function for the client

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="27cd1472-d25b-433c-9976-fd5161a36f1a">inline function</dfn>

When the compiler copies the function code in line at the point of each invocation

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="12ca450a-86e6-4a12-9ae5-edd066ca0868">local variable</dfn>

A variable declared inside a function

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="6b616769-5e5f-4048-afd9-9f2d975aa665">parameter</dfn>

Variables defined in the function signature

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="9f631c77-01b5-4ee0-8502-7c892b6e7043">parameter list</dfn>

Features that define the function

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="afe4f4ef-7932-4b24-9666-6a4b24758000">pass-by-reference</dfn>

A term used when the address of the actual parameter is passed to the function

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="12c253eb-2f8a-4439-a4d6-1826966a502a">pass-by-value</dfn>

A term used when a copy of the value of the argument is passed to the function

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="ccbf75b0-6fb8-4609-8311-0e35f9e8d724">reference variable</dfn>

A function parameter that references the original variable.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="7e3d4005-209d-45ce-82bd-85b879b67302">return type</dfn>

The type for the return value of a function

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b63a4670-daa3-451a-8edc-0187fbfd5876">return value</dfn>

A value returned from a function using the return statement

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f58c9ff8-5d4c-4762-b731-0e8baf40db29">scope of variable</dfn>

The portion of the program where the variable can be accessed

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="667822f6-9981-4a84-bdcd-fd940fd884f1">static local variable</dfn>

A variable whose value is retained for use in the next function call

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b488d198-5e31-4e5c-b14e-7533c7cb1341">stepwise refinement</dfn>

A strategy for writing a large program that decomposes the program into subproblems. The subproblems can be further decomposed into smaller, more manageable problems. See also "[divide and conquer](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DB63)."

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="ffe22ad4-dcb0-4884-9423-79d53a6ffdd7">stub</dfn>

A simple but incomplete version of the function. Stubs enable testing for invoking the function from a caller.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="166ed5c6-3f77-4b9b-a309-6de1156f2fe4">top-down implementation</dfn>

Implementing and testing functions incrementally from the top along the chain of the functions

# Chapter 7

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="84f7324a-6428-44d5-9f33-4db3f3e3f324">array</dfn>

A data structure for storing a collection of data of the same type

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="60131af3-0312-4c36-b54a-7c7f3a57866d">array index</dfn>

An integer value that specifies the position of an element in the array. The array index is an int value starting with 0 for the first element, 1 for the second, and so on.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="9df8e56c-7031-4d83-98da-ec57586ebd82">array initializer</dfn>

A shorthand notation for creating and initializing an array

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="aa6297b4-f04c-4b53-a260-2c309b73e94c">array size declarator</dfn>

Specifies size of the array

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="df9ef789-437a-4714-9dac-6b34775bc6d3">binary search</dfn>

An efficient function to search a key in an array by comparing the key with the element in the middle of the array, reducing the search range by half. For binary search to work, the array must be pre-sorted.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="4d0cf6cc-62cd-4a23-899f-e59021587c94">C-string</dfn>

An array of characters ending with the null terminator '\0'

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b0553411-e38e-4c22-a247-826e74fc33a4">const array</dfn>

An array whose contents cannot be changed

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="8d37ade0-1e71-45d1-8291-0a6a0bd9bbd9">index</dfn>

To reference an element in an array

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f53c187c-08ed-4b5d-8507-49d80bf7e757">indexed variable</dfn>

Accesses an element in the array through an index via arrayRefVar[index]

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="acb293bd-66bd-41f0-b882-cc51eb17f4ea">linear search</dfn>

Compares the key with the element in the array sequentially.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="7cd5d6b5-e15d-4c89-87f9-49fccedaeb08">null terminator</dfn>

The last character in a C-string

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="27227160-012f-43e6-9ef9-90e0bdc3f08b">null terminator ('\0')</dfn>

The character at end of every C-string.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="39b912fd-d85c-43e5-96bb-b0f0150a0543">selection sort</dfn>

A sort that finds the largest number in the list and places it last. It then finds the largest number remaining and places it next to last, and so on until the list contains only a single number.

# Chapter 8

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f8679ac6-2df9-4429-8e61-9a586cc4f3f8">column index</dfn>

the index on the column in a two-dimensional array

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="88bf1896-d8af-473c-9f47-f87fc33e6b7a">n-dimensional arrays</dfn>

an array whose elements are accessed using multiple indices

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="2dec5c2c-13c7-42ef-8cd5-2c8762c88854">row index</dfn>

the index on the row in a two-dimensional array

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f9899035-31d4-493a-98ca-4e010e205158">two-dimensional array</dfn>

an array whose elements are accessed using two indices

# Chapter 9

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="90ccb815-11af-4642-8931-7c442e6822c8">abstract data type</dfn>

Another name for a class.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="473baa8b-bd76-449a-8a18-121c65b24f44">accessor</dfn>

A function that returns the value of a data field

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="9b1379b4-4ac7-4e02-a183-3058fea6d0cb">accessor function (getter)</dfn>

The function for retrieving a private field in an object

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="dad867f6-c371-433d-9200-62fd84751daa">action</dfn>

See "behavior"

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="11fd0440-a6a8-49cc-bd27-6836b6ea793e">anonymous object</dfn>

Created without a name and used once in the program.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="fb841ce8-a0e0-4ee4-9f01-8e59a73ada53">attribute</dfn>

A variable that stores a value for an object

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="fe37a2a5-639f-4b1d-bfb2-2f24d479601e">binary scope resolution operator (::)</dfn>

Qualifies the scope for a member in a class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="1d015b0f-d0ec-449a-94bb-4e311c66e477">calling object</dfn>

An object that invokes a function

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="00d88c9f-c854-468b-967f-39017abca646">class</dfn>

An encapsulated collection of data and functions that operate on data. A class may be instantiated to create an object.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="fef17095-6ecd-430a-a412-856eae395322">class abstraction</dfn>

A technique in software development that hides detailed implementation. Class abstraction hides the implementation of the class from the client. If the implementation changes, the client program will not be affected.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f0485084-4d9f-4ade-b029-03178dfe6e07">class encapsulation</dfn>

Combining of functions and data into a single data structure

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="9d930881-2c32-4a71-8296-7e73f841e4d0">class’s contract</dfn>

The collection of functions and fields that are accessible from outside a class, together with the description of how these members are expected to behave.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e4e15bf5-5c49-4315-8495-c806b25d678c">client</dfn>

The program that uses the a class.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="ec37ce1e-a32a-494d-8902-0ecc55a2f5ab">constructor</dfn>

A special function for initializing objects when creating objects using the new operator. The constructor has exactly the same name as its defining class. Constructors can be overloaded, making it easier to construct objects with different initial data values.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c1e7930e-cce9-498a-af84-14d0bb3ced2d">contract</dfn>

The class definition

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="74355c6c-87ac-45ec-93e2-e7c7784cdc58">data field</dfn>

See "[attribute](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DBEA)"

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="bedc7016-174f-4856-be6b-aa15864e2682">data field encapsulation</dfn>

Declaring a field private to prevent direct modifications of properties through the object reference by use of a private modifier.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="5abf874a-c286-42d7-bb59-3b7fe1340d6f">default constructor</dfn>

Occurs when a class does not define any constructors explicitly and a no-arg constructor with empty body is assumed.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="cac1f650-a3d6-4ebb-a8d7-86d364d6e997">directive #ifndef</dfn>

the directive to prevent multiple inclusion of header files

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="81df6bb0-19f8-4b7d-8bfb-6a4a40f099f7">dot operator (.)</dfn>

Accesses members of an object. If the member is static, it can be accessed through the class name using the dot operator.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c06515a6-767d-472a-8cad-7091ac0784ca">inclusion guard</dfn>

Prevents the inclusion of multiple header files by using the #ifndef directive.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="7ddef64a-36db-4958-97bf-4ab9044a1b9a">inline definition</dfn>

When the compiler copies the function code in line at the point of each invocation.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="7c1296ae-6736-45f7-8abd-1ef8aa1d579a">instance</dfn>

An object of a class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b26f0cf0-bb15-4b5a-acad-802744fb3417">instance function</dfn>

A nonstatic function in a class. Instance functions belong to instances and can only be invoked by them.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b0069e00-1d30-4913-a90c-a61550078836">instance variable</dfn>

A nonstatic data member of a class. An instance variable belongs to an instance of the class.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="bd938938-1f34-4010-8100-15859a42929f">instantiation</dfn>

The process of creating an object of a class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="68593bed-2fa4-45f2-8983-17de0aeef15c">member access operator</dfn>

Permits access to a member in an object

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="19552c74-1cf9-41dd-8d4d-c7bda2ba5a6b">member function</dfn>

An instance function in a class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f472dcfb-4e68-4ad8-86d1-177e63668a78">mutator</dfn>

The same as a setter function that places a new value in a data field

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a07afdc9-4b33-4d18-a023-db3d8e8b309d">mutator function (setter)</dfn>

A function to set a property in an object

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="55be2e43-0341-44fe-b5c9-2e712412c1af">no-arg constructor</dfn>

A constructor without arguments

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="3e6a8e65-1521-462e-8287-669705c52ec2">object</dfn>

An instance of a class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d26d2b08-1dde-4e08-85d1-666dc5c44119">object-oriented programming (OOP)</dfn>

An approach to programming that involves organizing objects and their behavior into classes of reusable components.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="dd8fc4a8-2b2f-47d7-9d8b-dbde7cda6263">private</dfn>

A modifier for members of a class. A private member can only be referenced inside the class.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="11fe0d6c-87df-4c9f-9dc6-608d0d070340">property</dfn>

Represented using a data field

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="4d0610fb-2db3-460f-8262-8a19a717b591">public</dfn>

A modifier for classes, data, and functions that can be accessed by all programs

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="eadc2da1-8a06-4d2f-b406-a4c1b8ae81c9">scope resolution operator (::)</dfn>

Specifies the class for the functions and constructors

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a1d6049c-0601-42ba-9b7b-7e393c636a86">state</dfn>

The current values of data fields in an object

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="236b8b2d-4c3a-4a6e-bc37-a0fc2061ea60">UML class diagram</dfn>

A graphical notation for describing classes

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="1fd8b8c0-aa54-45de-ab87-776e26da040a">Unified Modeling Language (UML)</dfn>

A graphical notation for describing classes and their relationships

# Chapter 10

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="375954f0-cdcf-4f9a-afc7-548e109e7a7c">aggregation</dfn>

A special form of association that represents an ownership relationship between two classes

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="53d70876-f2d6-4e18-80e6-81b7581c9071">composition</dfn>

A form of relationship that represents exclusive ownership of the class by the aggregated class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="9605735b-6da5-4b94-bf68-e4c525071818">constant function</dfn>

A member function that does not change the value of the object

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="51b3efb3-4f67-42b7-a377-5aefc2418da2">constructor initializer list</dfn>

Allows for data fields to be initialized.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="ccef6306-795d-441c-98be-702d15b2710e">has-a relationship</dfn>

See "[composition](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DC59)"

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="3044858b-5eb4-4304-a07c-a33592c01397">immutable class</dfn>

A class that contains all private data fields and no mutator functions and no accessor functions that would return a reference to a mutable data field object.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="ff90c0ac-92f4-444c-bbf5-66a2a043d0ff">immutable object</dfn>

The contents of the object cannot be changed

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="2af3f367-ebf5-4377-918b-5eee4fd7af03">include guard</dfn>

A C++ directive to avoid duplicate inclusion of the header files

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="0c27b474-3302-491d-af5b-aa79ac2c1664">instance data field</dfn>

A field that describes property

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="6dcc8e14-84dc-47ff-96a5-c94729cea110">instance field</dfn>

A data member belongs to an object. Each object has its independent value.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c9a0d9c4-ffc2-45cc-ae68-8cef94066620">instance function</dfn>

A function that must be invoked from an object

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="613158d2-6257-4552-931c-a0e34c528f86">instance variable</dfn>

A nonstatic data member of a class and belonging to an instance of the class.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="00b03f27-74eb-4096-9fa9-e55361a2f973">multiplicity</dfn>

A number or an interval that specifies how many of each class’s objects are involved in the relationship.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d6e5171c-bb6d-499e-bfcb-8274bfcb9fe3">mutator function (setter)</dfn>

A function that changes the value of a private field in an object

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="7ab13d29-9a80-4271-9dbd-c9d444c8b5ca">software life cycle</dfn>

Analysis, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e1c2794c-300a-4cfd-95f7-56d58a272d8a">static field</dfn>

A data member declared using the static modifier. A static variable is shared by all instances of that class. Static variables are used to communicate between different objects of the same class and to handle global states among these objects.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="ba5a4ff7-9651-4aed-891e-d1540b7ef780">static function</dfn>

A function that can be invoked without creating an instance of the class. To define static functions, put the modifier static in the function declaration.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d0b7182a-82b0-4b7e-87ed-80240525e39e">static variable</dfn>

A data field that is shared by all objects of the class

# Chapter 11

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a4377bca-1761-4a99-9dba-91b7b80a81e7">address operator</dfn>

The C++ operator & for obtaining the address of a variable

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="0bbb07b9-4cfe-473c-b0f0-4de54c1113d0">address operator (&)</dfn>

The address operator (&) returns the address of a variable

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="3a9b88fe-a90f-49fe-baaa-575339a0a10f">arrow operator (->)</dfn>

The operator for accessing the object through a pointer

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a7a50fa7-637a-4a72-a86e-a705e39a42e0">constant pointer</dfn>

Indicates that the pointer cannot be changed to point to a new address

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="7ad4203f-6a77-4f18-839b-860ed33fb4cc">copy constructor</dfn>

A special constructor in each class that is used to create an object initialized with another object’s data

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d1f020fd-03a9-42e0-9b4e-cf3afae17899">dangling pointer</dfn>

Indicates that the pointer points to a dynamic memory that has been freed

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d4b03d40-cc86-4749-86ff-47887c66bcf6">deep copy</dfn>

When cloning an object and all its fields are cloned recursively

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="beb0ad65-2326-4cae-a2e1-c294029eed4b">delete operator</dfn>

Removes a dynamically created variable

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="98bc3704-8421-4083-bf7f-76bb6abc5f68">dereference operator</dfn>

The C++ operator *pointer for accessing the value in a variable through a pointer

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="626ab3b6-77e4-4b70-9437-3de83ebd8f69">dereference operator (*)</dfn>

The operator that returns the value from a memory reference by a pointer

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e090ae0c-a53f-4c6c-b026-9f3818b8ce30">destructor</dfn>

Invoked when an object is created and a destructor is invoked when the object is destroyed. Every class has a default destructor if the destructor is not explicitly defined.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="fb17b9e1-71f8-4978-8174-873fcab618c7">freestore</dfn>

See "[heap](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DCB3)"

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="67328f88-ea74-48d2-b849-2150779f5a51">heap</dfn>

Memory space for storing dynamically created variables

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="60eead07-3707-40ce-9953-75d932331393">indirection operator</dfn>

See "[dereference operator](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DCA7)"

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="5fbd0000-d6d1-474c-bf0e-344e204cf495">memory leak</dfn>

Occurs when a dynamically created variable is not referenced and its content cannot be accessed but also cannot be discarded.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="ae6c5109-42a4-4d5f-a5cf-cea82e0ce8de">new operator</dfn>

The C++ operator for creating a variable dynamically

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c70e11a2-74ef-4137-ad1e-c6a8f0e7b282">pointer</dfn>

Stores the address of a variable in the memory

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="9b6a2486-946b-4653-ad5a-df942b39b7ec">pointer-based string</dfn>

See "[C-string](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DBC0)"

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="2688655c-fded-4f4f-a8da-d8af84e97045">shallow copy</dfn>

Occurs when cloning an object and fields that are a reference type do not have data members copied.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="37be724d-f074-4fcb-a952-17e45fb0d2c5">this</dfn>

A keyword that refers to the object itself

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c45ee73d-4f90-41ff-ab15-89a32340f260">this keyword</dfn>

A pointer that points to a calling object

# Chapter 12

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="ceebaeb7-dcd9-4202-b25f-01819a754bde">nullptr</dfn>

A keyword that represents a null pointer

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="5dfda19f-5f51-4f80-90ee-a8bdd8feaa8a">smart pointer</dfn>

A new feature in C++ automatic recollect

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="480c8422-a45f-41cd-ab5c-d6c3d03bd11a">stack</dfn>

A special type of the list where insertions and deletions take place only at the one end, referred to as the top of a stack

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d11f2b4d-e589-47ff-8bab-aa254d90af3a">template</dfn>

Defines generic functions and classes. Templates provide the capability to parameterize types in functions and classes.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="4d87d351-b5bc-41a4-96ae-7ddb538e0245">template class</dfn>

A generic class with generic types

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="96ca561f-ed7c-4046-a9ec-f161ba88bfbf">template function</dfn>

A generic function with generic types

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c354de6c-f523-4914-ab44-84d1510c1534">template prefix</dfn>

Specifies generic types before a class or function

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a1d6c9af-eb3c-44bc-a07a-55ebabe7fee8">type parameter</dfn>

Generic type

# Chapter 13

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="bf61c92b-79c4-4c50-b31d-cf8d0387e1a7">absolute file name</dfn>

Complete file name with drive letter such as c:\example\Test.cpp

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="40f08ef2-c1a3-4ff1-b2ac-a8a1189688ee">binary file</dfn>

Stores raw data that is not encoded

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="25250799-7651-4e1b-bfff-37b414165edc">binary I/O</dfn>

Interprets data as raw binary values

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="0e380106-c235-4418-8128-e04e799dbb87">file open mode</dfn>

Specifies how to open the file (such as input, output, append, or binary)

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="9c18c1d5-cd14-48c3-bee0-bc1da4e82629">file pointer</dfn>

An internal pointer to point to the read and write location in a file.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a11bb72d-8db3-44a8-95af-605687456238">fstream</dfn>

File stream class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e904ce5a-1b4b-442f-a62b-71fec9ff7dbd">ifstream</dfn>

Input file stream class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="41943d5b-6151-413d-859b-3ce833ca170a">input stream</dfn>

Obtains input

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="af72a86e-0087-4347-b5f0-6de4565eceac">ofstream</dfn>

Input file stream class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d6f6dd13-4575-42b4-8bbc-f19c6c14c2e3">output stream</dfn>

Performs file output

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="87520b76-0214-42a0-b06e-5e9c794fedf9">random access file</dfn>

The file that can be both read and written in any order

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="bd2a73ee-5b4c-4694-804e-68ec39921e46">relative file name</dfn>

File names with drive letters

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="744f21eb-e108-4b30-ac9d-1011d8ec26be">sequential access file</dfn>

The file is read or written sequentially from beginning to end

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c715f87f-213a-4170-abe7-ff08d449c139">stream</dfn>

An object that facilitates input or output. For input, it is called an input stream. For output, it is called an output stream.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="df91370d-6de2-4d1b-a6da-c007efa9f22f">stream state</dfn>

Indicates the state of the stream such as end, error, etc.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="099897e4-4c07-4254-ae5b-d3741976d657">text file</dfn>

A file that can be viewed by a text editor. The contents stored in a text file are characters that use an encoding scheme.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="749cd631-2cd1-4505-9e68-dc56e15ccad7">text I/O</dfn>

Interprets data in sequences of characters

# Chapter 14

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e3149ddb-6481-4570-9246-befeefe3e60b">friend class</dfn>

Can access private members of a class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="de4e51a1-2b76-491b-ac8a-a554cfb9b4b4">friend function</dfn>

A non-member function that can access private members of a class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="2c410659-a369-442f-af6b-74cddd306171">friend functions</dfn>

Allow a friend function to class A to access private members of class A

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e3313743-1363-40c2-b378-85a8703e3423">friend keyword</dfn>

The keyword to define a friend class or friend function

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="ed59d2e8-22e7-4f9a-a5b1-4989ea5441d4">Lvalue</dfn>

lvalue refers to a named item persists beyond a single expression.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="76e27769-e772-4a2f-bf20-bae7ab472268">rvalue</dfn>

rvalue refers to an unnamed value that disappears after it is used in the expression.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f98734af-a799-4c72-bf6c-88353449cf92">return-by-reference</dfn>

Functions as an alias to a variable by returning a reference.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f3bd0f95-272c-4ce2-a353-4f80b783fdb8">rule of three</dfn>

The copy constructor, the = assignment operator, and the destructor; also known as the Big Three

# Chapter 15

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c511d901-6d93-40ab-be1a-cf702ada8534">abstract class</dfn>

A superclass declared by using the abstract modifier that does not have any specific common features shared by subclasses. Unlike regular classes, instances cannot be created.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="5902f02f-d8b0-407a-ba8b-c2e09ea7b2d3">abstract function</dfn>

A function signature without implementation. Its implementation is provided by its subclasses. An abstract function is denoted with an abstract modifier and must be contained in an abstract class. In a nonabstract subclass extended from an abstract class, all abstract functions must be implemented, even if they are not used in the subclass.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="3ba05e69-99c2-447e-85d7-5c72dfc15228">base class</dfn>

A class inherited by a subclass

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="86ead167-2331-4e0a-be78-e8ea91ab65d2">child class</dfn>

A derived class from a base class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="eb9a96c8-63d9-4d53-ac65-483ac762926b">constructor chaining</dfn>

When constructing an instance of a class invokes all the constructors, chaining base classes along the inheritance chain

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d70e9e90-c906-475d-99d5-0584657ab885">derived class</dfn>

A class that inherits from or extends a base class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="23283724-f619-451c-99da-866f637dfffd">destructor chaining</dfn>

When destructing an instance of a class invokes all the destructors along the inheritance chain with the derived class’s destructor invoked first

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="63ffd68f-5f3c-47f2-9bc4-f6e978a3e5c2">downcasting</dfn>

Casting an object from a superclass type to subclass

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e9788f78-996c-45cd-9bfb-c0ef656d46db">dynamic binding</dfn>

Implements the call for whether a function is defined in a superclass or overridden in a subclass during runtime.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e2aa23d7-4418-411f-9253-24fca4a4507d">generic programming</dfn>

Allows functions to be used generically for a wide range of object arguments through polymorphism

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d6f74825-094b-4f2a-8e56-910e2963dabb">inheritance</dfn>

Declares a new class by extending an existing class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="464ab174-7578-4c6d-b509-7e400c37cbc0">is-a relationship</dfn>

See "[inheritance](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DD58)"

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="6277b252-5c2b-4299-8e78-29db53bcc783">override</dfn>

In C++, redefines a virtual function in a derived class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="196bf4f8-c7b1-4193-842f-7d2f79331fb0">override function</dfn>

Redefines a virtual function

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="8c0ea519-d8c0-46f3-b48c-6439472ff3eb">parent class</dfn>

Serves as a base for defining a derived class and is the same as a base class.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="9af0aa82-9697-4792-8ddd-4cde681aed04">polymorphism</dfn>

Refers to the feature that an object of a subclass can be used by any code designed to work with an object of its superclass

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="7fd3d923-816e-432e-8306-34ea3b97f382">protected</dfn>

A modifier for members of a class. A protected member of a class can be used in the class in which it is declared or any subclass derived from that class.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="2ec56499-1fd8-4d5e-8b52-90d179d1e289">pure virtual function</dfn>

A function declaration without implementation. Also known as abstract function.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b2068315-28e8-41f7-a481-d5a362bdbd85">redefine</dfn>

To implement the function in a subclass that is declared in a superclass

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="1f80deeb-9fc2-47c4-9e45-1a2dc0742e36">subclass</dfn>

See "[derived class](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DD49)"

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="26a08a34-95ec-4fc0-be3f-fbc0fdd4168d">subtype</dfn>

A type defined by a derived class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="4d18d1ba-35e3-4857-877c-d72e8fcb9622">supclass</dfn>

See "[base class](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DD40)"

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a38dd649-43d7-4d0d-abeb-654a0e17e161">supertype</dfn>

A type defined by its base class

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="859cff2a-af68-4d7e-a7c2-52d94c444634">upcasting</dfn>

Casting an object from a subclass type to superclass

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="68280145-a250-4b31-a90d-933d4749b35b">virtual function</dfn>

A function declared with the keyword virtual. In C++, redefining a virtual function in a derived class is called overriding a function.

# Chapter 16

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e00f123e-3d0d-49d0-9fd5-cfa3486b4bb5">exception</dfn>

An unexpected event indicating that a program has failed in some way. They can be handled in a try-catch block.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="edb3aa1c-a8e6-4072-ba82-89ffafe3873e">exception specification</dfn>

The type of exception a function may throw

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="9be5ae95-c7b7-43e8-a8eb-5331639b9f25">rethrow exception</dfn>

After an exception has been caught in a catch clause, it may be reexamined and thrown again.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d777821a-e5be-41e4-af7a-1a60447aecc2">standard exception</dfn>

In C++, examples of common classes for exceptions include runtime_error and overflow_error

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="573810bf-ed61-46df-a618-8d68fd8548ad">throw exception</dfn>

A statement that indicates event failure. E.g., when an exception is raised, it is said to be "thrown."

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="0f0b0288-4363-40c0-81b6-1cbfd19b233e">throw list</dfn>

Defines a list of exceptions that may be thrown from a function

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="8d4b4cce-b1b2-4499-b090-325fd5c4d004">unchecked function</dfn>

In C++, a function that is invoked when an exception is thrown, but the exception is not declared in the exception specification.

# Chapter 17

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f8373cd8-f1ad-468a-8be9-325e76636329">base case</dfn>

A simple case where recursion stops

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="2550f531-4d31-47ae-8f9b-a772fb4fa793">infinite recursion</dfn>

Occurs when recursion never stops

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="85eecd98-db04-4c28-a622-881ee8a6e951">recursive function</dfn>

A function that invokes itself directly or indirectly

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a1e78d9d-b541-4e7c-b15b-837b94b2f891">recursive helper function</dfn>

Can be declared to modify the original function to receive parameters so it can be invoked recursively

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="22603c0f-7824-4a8a-bee8-df92118a0301">stopping condition</dfn>

See "[base case](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DDA0)"

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="2edadc46-10af-4cd3-b2ad-aef3b8be93ea">tail recursion</dfn>

Occurs when there are no pending operations to be performed on return from a recursive call

# Chapter 18

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="8ff94867-e29a-4774-a3d1-efa06e62db6a">average-case analysis</dfn>

An average-case analysis attempts to determine the average amount of time among all possible inputs of the same size

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="7f78db56-aff0-4a01-9f84-b0bd81bd8e05">backtracking approach</dfn>

Searches for a candidate solution incrementally, abandoning that option as soon as it determines that the candidate cannot possibly be a valid solution. It then looks for a new candidate.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="29d48099-d93c-45f2-95fa-1948da827734">best-case input</dfn>

An input that results in the shortest execution time

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="0f99f06b-2ea7-4014-9ff9-05a408db7440">best-time analysis</dfn>

The analysis to find the best-case time

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="5fc98dfd-1d16-41fb-ac58-877962f992e0">Big-O notation</dfn>

Comparing algorithms by examining their growth rates. In this notation, constants and smaller terms can be ignored in favor of focusing on dominating terms.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="bd8a1b84-42b2-45e6-9e7d-4871df123328">brute force</dfn>

An algorithmic approach that solves a problem in the simplest or most direct or obvious way

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="304bc733-52cc-4663-85ca-806b47b52504">constant time</dfn>

The Big-O notation estimates the execution time of an algorithm in relation to the input size. If the time is not related to the input size, the algorithm is said to take constant time with the notation 0(1).

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="35297370-a2ff-47ec-942a-1d2b6b3f1973">convex hull</dfn>

A polygon in which every line connecting two vertices is inside the polygon

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="90bc1335-f3fb-4608-9366-25274f1f203c">divide-and-conquer approach</dfn>

Divides the problem into subproblems, solves the subproblems, then combines the solutions of the subproblems to obtain the solution for the entire problem. Unlike the dynamic programming approach, the subproblems in the divide-and-conquer approach don’t overlap. A subproblem is smaller in size than the original problem and can be solved by applying recursion.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="eca14b6b-7281-4aff-b67f-196d8afdcb84">dynamic programming approach</dfn>

The process of solving subproblems, then combining the solutions of the subproblems to obtain an overall solution

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="21a0746d-9eab-4dbd-858b-7c476d2247af">exponential algorithm</dfn>

When execution time for an algorithm increases as the input size increases. It is notated as 0(Cn).

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d1b908a3-a1b3-42b4-9224-93b8562b8054">growth rate</dfn>

Measures how fast the time complexity of an algorithm grows as the input size grows

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="6ccde1ee-9a72-4d25-b689-31aa38cda02e">logarithmic time</dfn>

An algorithm with the 0(log n) time complexity

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="78cf4cf3-7849-4d4b-8294-e22332d404fe">quadratic time</dfn>

An algorithm with the 0(n2) time complexity

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e0c6313d-5192-45f7-833a-057b7b0ddda1">worst-case input</dfn>

An input that results in the longest execution time

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f2559e05-1213-4ba7-81bd-b3abd82987dc">worst-time analysis</dfn>

The analysis to find the worst-case time

# Chapter 19

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="34e46b5d-3567-4637-aaaf-4433ee9770b1">bubble sort</dfn>

An algorithm that makes several passes through the array. On each pass, successive neighboring pairs are compared. If a pair is in decreasing order, its values are swapped; otherwise, the values remain unchanged. Smaller values gradually "bubble" their way to the top and the larger values sink to the bottom.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="89231f28-634f-46aa-a884-584fb5bc3547">bucket sort</dfn>

A sort wherein each bucket labeled in the range from 0 to N-1 holds elements with the same key value.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="2f868c1a-d14d-4ab0-94ae-9cd3bb534906">complete binary tree</dfn>

A binary tree with every level full. If the last level is not full, its leaves are placed leftmost on that level.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="62747058-af92-448c-8500-09ec058ee55b">external sort</dfn>

Sort data stored in an external file

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c395a891-83da-43fe-ab71-ab5d32ed61af">heap</dfn>

Memory space for storing dynamically created variables

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="7f96f567-4daa-4319-99b7-8e6f8cbe601b">heap sort</dfn>

A binary heap that sorts an array

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b17dd48c-ba8a-4c50-acbf-940893ef467e">height of a heap</dfn>

The height of a heap binary tree

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="0c3f4487-9998-43e4-9d23-aa1675786ea9">insertion sort</dfn>

An algorithm that sorts a list of values by repeatedly inserting a new element into a sorted sublist until the whole list is sorted

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="479e7e11-f695-49f1-ba09-9b17098c42c1">merge sort</dfn>

This algorithm divides an array into two halves and applies merge sort on each half recursively. After the two halves are sorted, they can be merged.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="417e6143-f909-4216-812a-ae8b35150fad">quick sort</dfn>

Developed by C. A. R. Hoare (1962), this algorithm selects an element, called the pivot, in the array and divides the array into two parts such that all the elements in the first part are less than or equal to the pivot and all the elements in the second part are greater than the pivot. The algorithm recursively applies apply the quick sort algorithm to the first part and then the second part.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="5f6981aa-bfc8-41d6-93a4-f8339194fd6b">radix sort</dfn>

A bucket sort based on radix

# Chapter 20

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c2bd830b-6f73-4cd7-90f7-6b2d75e545b3">circular doubly linked list</dfn>

A doubly linked list where the forward pointer of the last node points to the first node and the backward pointer of the first pointer points to the last node

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a0c88472-089e-4855-9b7e-ec6e98d2bbbb">circular linked list</dfn>

A singly linked list where the pointer of the last node points back to the first node

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d82b462d-f48d-4ce4-a10f-a087c520ce79">circular singly linked list</dfn>

A linked list whose last node links to its first node

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="4174ff79-03d3-4006-bf70-2fdfc87b69fd">dequeue</dfn>

To remove an element from a queue

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="cfa830be-10fb-4cf6-a52a-9f3e6fd0d800">doubly linked list</dfn>

Contains nodes with two pointers, one pointing to the next node and one pointing to the previous node, that are able to be traversed both forward and backward. These two pointers are called a forward pointer and a backward pointer.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="af6cdeb7-3db1-4031-a77b-9d82e13100df">endeque</dfn>

A queue operation to append an element to the queue

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="7bcb27e9-191b-42f6-8bd1-8c6fd26e2038">linked list</dfn>

A list where each element is contained in a structure called the node. All the nodes, one for each unique element, are chained through pointers.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="6cf3beb0-85ca-46fb-8e65-89c27dccd951">peek</dfn>

A stack operation to read the top element

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="8da6cb10-84f3-462c-be2c-fbac0cb94a3d">priority queue</dfn>

Occurs when elements are assigned with priorities and the element with the highest priority is accessed or removed first.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="47478710-1091-4189-a832-97131827d9dc">push</dfn>

A stack operation to add an element to the top

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="5507b770-cf37-47bc-b1b6-46d47bbc9772">queue</dfn>

Represents a waiting list, where insertions take place at the back (also referred to as the tail) and deletions take place from the front (also referred to as the head)

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="9874b718-58ee-424f-8b93-b0498bdc288c">singly linked list</dfn>

See "[linked list](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DE1E)"

# Chapter 21

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a4693df0-b962-40e2-9de6-fab6a5e0dfee">binary search tree</dfn>

A binary tree with no duplicate elements. For every node in the tree, the value of any node in its left subtree is less than the value of the node and the value of any node in its right subtree is greater than the value of the node.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e15069f4-16b1-49ce-b54c-b84206f19bec">binary tree</dfn>

A data structure to support searching, sorting, inserting, and deleting data efficiently

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="ab954e50-d0a2-4907-99f3-9dbd3693ce4a">inorder traversal</dfn>

Visiting the left subtree of the current node first, then the current node itself, and finally the right subtree of the current node

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="9ac79c3a-192c-4c2e-8eed-df60cb9df6d3">postorder traversal</dfn>

Visiting the left subtree of the current node first, then the right subtree of the current node, and finally the current node itself

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="fb95edb2-bbe6-48b2-b718-b1870a6e4a70">preorder traversal</dfn>

Visiting the current node first, then the left subtree of the current node, and finally the right subtree of the current node

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="1768b912-97e5-42c0-b4c4-92bf7c72dd70">tree traversal</dfn>

A process of visiting each node in the tree exactly once

# Chapter 22

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="048a063b-ce6b-4404-893d-6c042f04d310">associative container</dfn>

Non-linear containers that store sets of values or key/value pairs and can locate elements stored in the container quickly. The four associative containers are set, multiset, map, and multimap.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="1217fbff-53fc-4e27-a181-dfb6c7beb235">auto-type inference</dfn>

Uses the keyword auto to declare a type, wherein the compile automatically discovers the actual type in the context

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="9d7bb4cf-8c6c-4d2b-b701-445206482e54">bidirectional iterator</dfn>

A forward iterator with the capability of moving backward. The iterator can be moved freely back or forth one at a time.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="010ba2e8-bf47-4d0f-8729-99840ce57cbb">container</dfn>

Classes in the STL wherein a container object such as a vector is used to store a collection of data, often referred to as elements

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="80bb5a56-e52d-48f2-88c3-fe343de764cb">container adapter</dfn>

Constrained versions of sequence containers for handling special cases. The three container adapters are stack, queue, and priority_queue.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="3d5f694b-d742-4baa-a536-c830882108fc">deque</dfn>

The term deque stands for double-ended queue. A deque provides efficient operations to support insertion and deletion on both ends.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d4dee77c-f814-4137-b7c4-a1d1c11a5a32">first-class container</dfn>

Sequence containers and associative containers

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f3668a07-b17c-43fd-b2aa-622c0e5e4ec7">forward iterator</dfn>

Combines all the functionalities of input and output iterators to support both read and write operations

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c5b00fda-1ff5-4cfc-9ead-b7548e459f4d">input iterator</dfn>

Reads an element from a container. It can move only in a forward direction one element at a time.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="66a6915a-f153-411b-83da-52d5b014e864">istream_iterator</dfn>

Reads an element from the console

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="2e4250f5-7101-4d46-84fd-f3855548c466">iterator</dfn>

Similar to a pointer, used extensively in the first-class containers for accessing and manipulating the elements

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="3c1a8ddf-a21e-4608-b951-6a83f39bae25">list</dfn>

Implemented as a doubly-linked list that supports efficient insertion and deletion operations

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d7d10e6d-a19e-4102-8264-75f2de4d0fcd">map</dfn>

Provides quick access to each pair value using the key.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="7c99d2c6-7fa9-465f-8256-9404097acf18">multimap</dfn>

Similar to a map, except that a multimap allows duplicate keys

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c709fcea-38c7-4252-93f0-50bbd66c1b7c">multiset</dfn>

Stores elements and may contain duplicates

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="3eb26431-0188-4f7f-92a1-e7f68f0eb106">ostream_iterator</dfn>

Outputs an element to the console

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="fae6ff98-dc63-4cd2-b0c3-c3aa9ca05285">output iterator</dfn>

Writes an element to a container

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="bc566cbd-ae98-48e0-9ceb-bd611072445e">priority_queue</dfn>

A queue that removes an element iwith the highest priority

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d7d2e27e-f22f-44c4-8fc4-32449396a706">queue</dfn>

A first-in/first-out STL container

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="165e1b8a-b36c-4136-bd3f-19d75ec6507f">random-access iterator</dfn>

A bidirectional iterator with the capability of accessing any element in any order, i.e., jumping forward or backward by a number of elements

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="7cf85452-1036-4964-99cf-78553c65b42d">sequence container</dfn>

Represents linear data structures. The three sequence containers are vector, list, and deque (pronounced deck).

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a31c5172-dffb-4621-97c2-1e98bbd9b15c">set</dfn>

An STL associative container storing nonduplicate elements.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="168623c0-48e0-4256-b1d5-b89b68b68c62">STL algorithm</dfn>

In functions, manipulates data such as sorting, searching, and comparing elements

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="bd0e1297-4220-4754-9758-e9dbf9e7b9a7">vector</dfn>

A C++ class that represents a resizable array

# Chapter 23

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="4e9ae26b-cfcd-40f6-9771-9fb2550d812f">accumulate algorithm</dfn>

Obtains the sum of the elements in a range from the beginning iterator to the ending iterator

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="52acf74d-424d-4519-b0a4-0bcc3a05fa5b">adjacent_difference algorithm</dfn>

Creates a sequence of elements in which the first element is the same as the first element in the input sequence, and each subsequent element is the difference between the current element and the previous one.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="1e4010c2-9b11-4d4c-b04f-feb091d9645b">adjacent_find algorithm</dfn>

Searches for the first occurrence of adjacent elements of equal value or satisfying boolFunction(element)

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="9172c80c-a6e4-4ade-b2e5-9eecc93bcf62">binary_search algorithm</dfn>

Performs a binary performs a binary search in a sorted sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="6c246463-d523-426b-a030-357945ec445a">copy algorithm</dfn>

Duplicates the values in a sequence to another sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="2056bd63-09ef-4e32-a4b8-858414d9d695">count algorithm</dfn>

Determines the occurrence of a value in a sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="6111b116-05d6-48bd-827e-ea0299cb30e8">count_if algorithm</dfn>

Determines the occurrence of values in a sequence that satisfies a condition

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="79c3ee4f-61ce-4dc3-94b2-7746b28bd76f">fill algorithm</dfn>

Fills a container with a value in a specified sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b514e64b-ec2a-460e-b1fa-eb4070cc4f3c">fill_n algorithm</dfn>

Fills a container with n number of values

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="03a31f21-6c96-4edb-8e3d-581ae5f7a69c">find algorithm</dfn>

Finds the first-matching value in a sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="ac010dcf-4880-420e-a959-2e5e7fdcf831">find_end algorithm</dfn>

Finds the last-matching value in a sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e944a15e-2d03-41db-81ac-55b3b2941952">find_first_of algorithm</dfn>

Finds the first matching element in two sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b9eafe98-1f87-46c8-876a-ebd8a2fde36b">find_if algorithm</dfn>

Finds a value that matches a condition in a sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="90deb130-6155-4d79-a330-368d0e329b77">for_each algorithm</dfn>

Processes each element in a sequence by applying a function

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="72e483aa-9e89-4176-af06-b81b35576038">function object</dfn>

Functions used in STL algorithms

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="96b61bf0-d6b7-4d54-9f58-de29335498fd">generate algorithm</dfn>

Fills values in a sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="6388bd9f-8a1c-40e0-99d3-35b30bf6a423">generate_n algorithm</dfn>

Fills n number of values in a sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="4357c8e8-8e11-493f-bb09-07539a63194f">heap algorithms</dfn>

Provides heap operations for binary heaps

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="2e9d9970-e3d0-491b-976e-59335ab9b5cd">includes algorithm</dfn>

Tests whether a sequence contains another sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="76b3b7b1-4803-4153-b7ad-2e2c5fb3d1f7">inner_product algorithm</dfn>

Multiplies two sequences

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c8b2f077-7d94-4c79-9b6e-7f7ccdfdec8e">inplace_merge algorithm</dfn>

Merges the first part of the sequence with the second part; assume that the two parts contain sorted consecutive elements.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="56886cf3-36a3-4322-93da-4502d02415fa">iter_swap algorithm</dfn>

Swaps the values pointed to by the iterators

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="40fc79c4-3eb5-4a81-ba19-9aa8a3a05a42">max_element algorithm</dfn>

Returns the iterator of the maximum element

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c00b8e75-23d8-4660-8221-961f0755fa05">merge algorithm</dfn>

Merges two sorted sequences

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="25518742-2e71-4fb8-aae7-20473da6d3a8">min_element algorithm</dfn>

Returns the iterator of the maximum element

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="1d2179b4-f812-4d89-915c-a823796da4cd">modifying STL algorithms</dfn>

Change the elements in the container by insertion, removing, rearranging, and changing the values of the elements

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a67ae680-96fa-40f2-9834-0eab249a047d">nonmodifying STL algorithms</dfn>

Do not change the contents in the container. They obtain information from the elements.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b56fc172-b696-4f16-aa2b-4aa38317f859">numeric STL algorithms</dfn>

Provide four numeric operations for computing accumulate, adjacent difference, inner product, and partial sum

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b8e17612-55ac-479e-b229-157b85daebf4">partial_sum algorithm</dfn>

Creates a sequence in which each element is the sum of all the preceding elements.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="faa519b5-cee7-44d4-9c3b-cdc06fe2cafb">random_shuffle algorithm</dfn>

Reorders the elements in a sequence at random

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="6f16bee3-f3e5-40b1-8e44-9494181d765e">remove algorithm</dfn>

Deletes elements from a sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d6e3b0e4-0f33-4471-8295-ae98e271953b">remove_copy algorithm</dfn>

Copies all the elements in the sequence in a source sequence to the target container

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c1aa91a3-bf69-439c-89f3-3c77ce81822b">remove_copy_if algorithm</dfn>

Copies all the elements in the sequence in a source sequence to the target container that satisfies conditions

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="4fc95f91-9aec-4528-8398-98ade8cd48cc">remove_if algorithm</dfn>

Deletes elements in the sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="5f83a150-e55c-4ae7-9fcb-1e178a4ae6af">replace algorithm</dfn>

Replaces elements in the sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="2fe6444a-df86-49cb-8eb2-8fab55c2340c">replace_copy algorithm</dfn>

Replaces elements in the sequence and copies to the target container

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="1b9b2de2-0dea-40f2-8592-174433be4f59">replace_copy_if algorithm</dfn>

Replaces elements in the sequence that satisfy a condition and copies to the target container

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="dea6468c-9c73-4a14-9a63-eeb0156de3f7">replace_if algorithm</dfn>

Replaces elements in the sequence that satisfy a condition

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a65e2e6b-8c8c-488b-b0e4-3f027eaf7667">reverse algorithm</dfn>

Reverses the elements in a sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b83493ba-a2c8-4ae5-a555-57bffca4eba3">reverse_copy algorithm</dfn>

Reverses the elements in a sequence and copies to the target container

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="6adbcc67-97e2-40b0-ac70-7ef76f3ca41c">rotate algorithm</dfn>

Rotates the elements in a sequence. It specifies a subsequence and places it to the beginning of the sequence.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="3a392b01-70e6-4c66-a72e-e54fc5435d2b">rotate_copy algorithm</dfn>

Rotates the elements in a sequence and copies to the target container

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="70732cd9-b955-4833-9dae-eaa8e7476fb7">search algorithm</dfn>

Searches within an element in a sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="dc7c1f35-cb8e-44db-8158-117b79c49806">search_n algorithm</dfn>

Searches for consecutive occurrences of a value in the sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e0f39ad9-9098-4918-8df7-67b2e09ac744">set_difference algorithm</dfn>

Performs set difference for two sequences

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="4e2eadda-63de-42bd-9082-93a0045bac34">set_intersection algorithm</dfn>

Performs set intersection for two sequences

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="6fd9c2ce-ae73-41ab-8cc2-e9b28e0bd36f">set_symmetric_difference algorithm</dfn>

Obtains the elements that appear in either sequence, but not in both

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="6362dd48-3c48-42e8-834e-98bd80c1c5de">set_union algorithm</dfn>

Performs set union for two sequences

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b1a1ff6b-42b8-41ac-9d0c-a091b114908a">sort algorithm</dfn>

Sorts a sequence

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="3c8c2dd0-3954-47eb-8fa0-52b5558f2996">swap algorithm</dfn>

Swaps two variables

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="3b0ca97e-11de-4830-9db7-72f87cc1f1dc">swap_range algorithm</dfn>

Swaps function swaps two sequences

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="aa3b34bc-7514-48cc-92e2-546e9806ca76">transform algorithm</dfn>

Applies a function on each element in the sequence and copy the result to a target sequence

# Chapter 24

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="30e7bb55-2aac-4561-8372-88f5a15e4c88">associative array</dfn>

An alternative term for map

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="8e496168-4602-41eb-9fef-b990474b13ad">cluster</dfn>

Groups of consecutive cells in the hash table during linear probing to be to be occupied.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="1b6519d6-21b3-45f4-82ad-d2ea9eacd301">dictionary</dfn>

See "[map](#glossary.xhtml_P700101309700000000000000004DE6C)"

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="33be209f-be8c-4c3e-8ab4-f27c0ae3609c">double hashing</dfn>

Uses a secondary hash function h'(key) on the keys to determine the increments to avoid the clustering problem

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="8aaf8ac6-603d-483e-8839-847e2d083b4b">hash code</dfn>

An integer value derived from an object

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="55c9ae0b-a3b5-417f-aac3-1e04fbd747c1">hash function</dfn>

The function that maps a key to an index in the hash table

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="af6f2edc-7f74-4013-b517-47060a29602d">hash map</dfn>

A map that is implemented using a hash table

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e12767df-d41d-46c8-b0d5-b70e3f34850b">hash set</dfn>

A set that is implemented using a hash table

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="98127565-bdfa-4b90-a2ff-8de6e6490ad2">hash table</dfn>

An array that stores the elements whose keys are mapped to an integers as the indexes of the array

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="16fc648f-59d7-4129-8627-c6d8cb2ef355">linear probing</dfn>

A technique for handling collision. When a collision occurs during the insertion of an entry to a hash table, linear probing finds the next available location sequentially.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="98aa8b74-85cb-4c67-b838-e4bca002b24b">load factor</dfn>

Measures how full a hash table is. It is the ratio of the number of elements to the size of the hash table.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="63e2f05e-eead-469f-987c-8e89946d8082">open addressing</dfn>

The process of finding an open location in the hash table in the event of collision

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="0aeefc0a-6238-465d-8a69-962b947494b9">perfect hash function</dfn>

A function that maps each search key to a different index in the hash table

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="267a9faf-8e1e-4d2d-bcdf-7b993f6285e0">polynomial hash code</dfn>

A function used for obtaining an integer value derived from an object

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="83ccd467-4e91-4b6f-8fab-c41e37686917">quadratic probing</dfn>

Avoids the clustering problem that can occur in linear probing by examining the cells at indices k + a quadratic number.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="9815a853-2d7a-41ea-bf02-f99d137c4e3a">rehashing</dfn>

When the load factor of a hash table is exceeded and reloaded into a new, larger hash table.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="d21a6316-2d36-40e2-955f-1d3b6df5126e">secondary clustering</dfn>

The clustering caused by quadratic probing

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="3fc67eb4-e4f1-451b-a4df-6969fa24b80f">separate chaining</dfn>

A hashing scheme that places all entries with the same hash index into the same location, rather than finding new locations. Each location in the separate chaining scheme is called a bucket, which is a container that holds multiple entries.

# Chapter 25

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="da70fd6c-6c0f-4552-9d49-6003de94bfe8">AVL tree</dfn>

A well-balanced binary tree where the difference between the heights of two subtrees for every node is 0 or 1.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="15e658e8-e840-4088-a917-2c5959cc3fff">balance factor</dfn>

The height of a node's right subtree minus the height of its left subtree

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="8c199de5-8a2d-464e-9b98-db1a36c7fbde">left-heavy</dfn>

A node with a balance factor of -1 or less

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="858cc209-701a-4ab6-bd4c-f44c81f29c51">LL rotation</dfn>

An LL imbalance occurs at a node A, such that A has a balance factor of -2 and a left child B with a balance factor of -1 or 0\. This type of imbalance can be fixed by performing a single right rotation at A.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c570ef26-c37b-4851-ab37-0a13e780f859">LR rotation</dfn>

An LR imbalance occurs at a node A, such that A has a balance factor of -2 and a left child B with a balance factor of +1\. Assume B’s right child is C. This type of imbalance can be fixed by performing a double rotation (first a single left rotation at B and then a single right rotation at A).

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e1d935cf-e0bd-4dff-afd9-69d25926f9ae">perfectly-balanced tree</dfn>

A complete binary tree

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b5cc555b-95f4-46c0-a869-59fc51ce5dce">right-heavy</dfn>

A node with a balance factor +1 or greater

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a04169f1-a431-4230-82c2-d97e352cce06">RL rotation</dfn>

An RL imbalance occurs at a node A, such that A has a balance factor of +2 and a right child B with a balance factor of -1\. Assume B’s left child is C. This type of imbalance can be fixed by performing a double rotation (first a single right rotation at B and then a single left rotation at A).

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="64d86f75-c605-4206-860d-af5c5c5664a8">rotation</dfn>

A process for rebalance a tree into an AVL tree

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="0c2051a7-5af6-4e92-9044-e44c7e7f73a9">RR rotation</dfn>

An RR imbalance occurs at a node A, such that A has a balance factor of +2 and a right child B with a balance factor of +1 or 0\. This type of imbalance can be fixed by performing a single left rotation at A.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a267bdc0-6b93-4061-bded-9e83fbcec193">well-balanced tree</dfn>

Occurs when the height of the subtrees for each node is about the same, or O(logn)

# Chapter 26

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="246b1318-b975-4ef7-99a6-f09d3f8600d4">adjacency list</dfn>

An array of lists. Each list [i] contains the vertices that are adjacent to i.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c0089a71-f8e9-407c-98fe-cad865e463ff">adjacency matrix</dfn>

Represents edges using a matrix

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="2de38f36-11b3-401d-985b-3395c7bebf95">adjacent vertices</dfn>

Two vertices in a graph connected by the same edge

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="777a1113-8c0b-4eee-b939-62d0efc69c8c">breadth-first search</dfn>

first visits a vertex, then all its adjacent vertices, then all the vertices adjacent to those vertices, and so on. It is recommended to skip a vertex if it has already been visited.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="b71ba049-8962-4e95-b0a8-554ab1fcb66b">complete graph</dfn>

A graph in which every two pairs of vertices are connected

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="de10e812-095b-4d55-9904-9cf5ebac3756">degree</dfn>

The number of edges incident to a vertex

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="ec85454a-98d5-4e4b-84eb-bdb97a10d299">depth-first search</dfn>

A search that first visits the root, then recursively visits the subtrees of the root

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="4d35933b-e84c-4048-9da3-b5c2ebfcb57d">directed graph</dfn>

A graph in which edges indicate where and in what way to move from one vertex through the other

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="8339093f-66df-4300-affa-137a186d3447">graph</dfn>

A mathematical structure that represents relationships among entities in the real world

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="8a38336f-4550-4ddd-a62b-5b88d0c43bb6">incident edge</dfn>

An edge in a graph that joins two vertices

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="539bd895-7db3-4920-a993-692fdf4416ec">parallel edge</dfn>

Two vertices connected by two or more edges

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="dbe3ecf6-312c-4b3d-87bc-edaece305854">Seven Bridges of Königsberg</dfn>

The first known problem solved using graph theory

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="f8a5a496-364b-4ca9-81b2-d626d12658ab">simple graph</dfn>

A graph that has no loops and parallel edges

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="3f2f6b7a-9242-4bc8-b901-a2f10728768a">spanning tree</dfn>

Within a graph; a subgraph that is a tree and connects all vertices in the graph.

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="90622d3d-7ec5-4017-81be-dbfc28319434">undirected graph</dfn>

A graph that has no directed edges

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="7f19b022-df11-471c-99ff-9cb891627b1e">unweighted graph</dfn>

Edges or vertices not assigned with weights

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="a062c655-e605-4f0b-8c05-f5cfc047d6e7">weighted graph</dfn>

Edges or vertices assigned with weights

# Chapter 27

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="dfb3c969-2560-4482-ab97-c0ea5676363d">Dijkstra’s algorithm</dfn>

A well-known algorithm for finding the shortest path from a single source to all other vertices in a weighted graph

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="e393c8e4-0258-40d4-978c-b1917759636d">edge-weighted graph</dfn>

Edges assigned with weights

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="55eae58c-629e-4a4d-92c8-4afe7376ae2d">minimum spanning tree</dfn>

A spanning tree with the minimum total weights

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="c6a2d040-15af-4651-8dec-3f3b17ce5ae8">Prim’s algorithm</dfn>

A well-known algorithm for finding a spanning tree in a connected weighted graph

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="2d76db29-6d54-4d94-a023-89b5b92b3721">shortest path</dfn>

A path between two vertices with the shortest total weight

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="6951125e-b761-47f5-984b-62464619e66b">single-source shortest path</dfn>

The shortest path from a source to all other vertices

<dfn data-chaucer-element-id="0881803c-cf72-4401-897f-59fb7422bcbc">vertex-weighted graph</dfn>

Weights assigned to vertices
